what_it_does: ROSE is a framework for managing large-scale surrogate modeling, where cheaper approximate models learn to predict results of expensive simulations. The core challenge is dynamically deciding what simulations to run, retraining the surrogate model with new data, and managing this loop across multiple supercomputers. ROSE uses active learning (automatically choosing the most informative simulations to run) and asynchronous execution so simulations on one machine can proceed while models train on another, dramatically reducing total wall-clock time.
